text:
samir: heads up — p95 decode latency spiked ~2x on the last canary after the kernel-priority-ladder roll (commit ab12f3). seeing a lot of short tool-invoke requests getting routed to fused kernels and paying swap cost.
maya: saw the graphs. is the ladder the one that biases toward fused_attn for seq>256?
samir: yeah. it uses our estimator -> preferred kernel funnel. the problem: structured outputs + toolcalls produce many short decodes with stop tokens and tool pauses, which causes frequent kernel swaps and KV resyncs. p50 roughly stable, p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~420ms, overall token/sec -12%.
eli: do we have flamegraphs or a profile dump?
perf-bot: collected 1m stack samples from canary group (top frames): fused_attn_kernel::setup() 31%, kernel_select::score_round() 19%, kv_cache::resync() 8%, memset/alloc 6% — kernel swap + cache churn dominate.
maya: that matches hypothesis. fused_attn has higher setup cost on short seqs; swapping in/out for toolcall bursts is expensive.
dani: quick mitigation idea: add a tool_pause_hint to request metadata and bias scheduler to keep those on the fast_generic kernel and lower the batch token target for them (less batching but lower swap churn). also consider pinning KV across pauses so resyncs don't force full rebuild.
eli: agree. propose two-part experiment: routing override + KV pin. routing config draft: 
```
heuristics:
  kernel_priority_ladder:
    enabled: true
    ladders:
      - min_seq: 256
        preferred_kernel: fused_attention_v2
  tool_call_overrides:
    pause_hint: true
    batch_target_tokens: 8
    kernel_fallback: generic_fast
```
maya: let's A/B 10% first. infra-bot can we deploy the change to the ab-test group?
infra-bot: ab-test config deployed to group B (0.1). hosts: pool-rt-2[3-6]. rollout id: rollout/ker-ladder-ab10.
samir: after ~30m: baseline p95 420ms, group B (override) p95 ~200ms, token/sec B +6%, throughput unchanged. kernel_swap_count/request dropped from 0.7 -> 0.12.
eli: promising. but we still see residual jitter in baseline due to mixed batches where non-tool and tool requests are batched together and cause mid-batch swap. need additional mitigations.
dani: opened PR #874 to pin KV for tool-hinted requests across the pause boundary (small memory overhead, avoids full resync).
perf-bot: regression triage summary: root causes = (1) increased freq of kernel swaps for short tool-invoke sequences, (2) KV cache resync on pause+resume, (3) ladder threshold placed too low for our split workload. mitigations prioritized: routing override, KV pin, raise ladder min_seq to 384, and add metrics for kernel_swap_count and kv_resync_count.
maya: can we add an alert for abnormal swap density? e.g., if kernel_swap_count/request > 1 for >0.5% of requests in a minute.
elI: yes. creating alert: ALERT-INF-ker-swap-density.
samir: also found some stop-token detector behavior: structured-output generator emits stop markers early causing toolcalls to restart short decodes frequently. eli, can you look at reducing premature stops inside structured chunks?
eli: on it. adding a small hysteresis window for stop detection inside structured-output blocks so we don't end the decode unless the stop is present for 2 consecutive tokens.
dani: once KV pin PR merges, I suggest canary to 20% then full rollback if p95 regresses. infra-bot, prepare rollback tag.
infra-bot: rollback tag available: rollback/kernel-ladder/ab12f3.
perf-bot: created issue INF-2104: "kernel swap jitter for tool-invokes" with attached perf traces and the above mitigation plan.
samir: thanks all — plan: (1) merge KV pin PR #874, (2) update ladder min_seq -> 384, (3) enable tool_pause_hint routing at 20% canary, (4) monitor new metrics for 2h, then decide. i'll post updates. :thumbsup:
